Ivy Nguyen: Heads-up — Neptune account spiked after enabling live embeddings + aggressive similarity indexing. Need a short QBR-ready remediation and a customer-friendly note. cc @Marco
Marco Silva: On it. 24h burn = $11.2k, projected 30d @ current = ~$336k. Their historical average ~ $60k/mo. Credits remaining = $42k, retainer = $25k/mo, retainer expires in 10 days.
Janelle Park: Do we know whether indexing or query cost is dominant? If indexing, we can propose staged ingestion + cheaper indexer variant.
Marco Silva: Indexing (background) = 72% of the spike, query path = 18%, other = 10%. They launched full reindex with concurrency 16 to finish migration faster.
Ivy Nguyen: Customer note should be empathetic: say we saw the spike, temporary mitigation options, and offer a free 30m enablement to dial-in ingest concurrency and batching.
Janelle Park: For the QBR slide: keep 3 bullets: what happened, what we did immediately, recommended next steps (enablement + commit ask). Also include runway scenario numbers.
Marco Silva: Draft budget guard snippet for slide: ```yaml
policy: neptune_budget_guard
soft_threshold_usd: 30000
hard_threshold_usd: 45000
soft_action: notify-cs + email-customer
hard_action: pause-indexing + swap-index-model
```
Ivy Nguyen: Good. Ops: can we do an automated fallback that swaps indexer to the quantized variant and drops concurrency to 4 when hard threshold hits?
ops-bot: Suggested fallback applied logically: set-model->open-embed-q4-8bit + concurrency=4. Expected indexing cost delta ~ -58%.
Marco Silva: Scenario forecasts (30d): status_quo = $336k, quantize+concurrency=4 = $155k, pause-reindex = $78k. Note: pause hurts onboarding SLA.
Janelle Park: CLI toggles for operations (short): ```bash
# quick throttle
rwctl jobs update --account NEPTUNE --job reindex --concurrency 4
# swap to quantized embed
rwctl accounts set-model --account NEPTUNE --route embeddings --model open-embed-q4-8bit --batch-size 64
# emergency pause
rwctl jobs pause --account NEPTUNE --job reindex
```
Ivy Nguyen: We'll add a tiny sparkline for runway and one-line customer-friendly remediation in the slide. Marco, can you confirm the expected percent cost reduction if we do quantize+concurrency?
Marco Silva: Expected drop ~54-60% for indexing path, overall 30d projection to $155k as above.
Janelle Park: Recommend we also offer a 14-day monitoring window post-tuning and auto-budget alerts: soft=50% credits, hard=80% credits, plus automated throttle at hard.
ae-bot: Account NEPTUNE: credits_remaining=42000, monthly_retainer=25000, retainer_expiry=2026-04-02, auto_renew=false. Notified AE.
finance-bot: Reminder: if customer accepts enablement + 30% staged commit increase, projected committed coverage drops to ~2 months runway vs status quo <1 month.
Ivy Nguyen: Action items: Marco - paste final numbers and tiny sparkline into the QBR slide by EOD. Janelle - prepare 2-line enablement invite and checklist. I'll draft customer note framing it as "predictability package" and lead renewal ask with AE. Meeting 16:30 to finalize.
Marco Silva: I'll upload numbers and a sparkline link here shortly.
Janelle Park: Enablement blurb ready: "30-minute ingest & cost stabilization workshop: we	will review ingestion concurrency, enable batching and model fallbacks, implement toggles, and monitor for 14 days."
Ivy Nguyen: Perfect. Last ask 00: capture 3 sample workflows from customer where latency matters so we can avoid regressing UX when batching. Janelle, please collect during enablement.
ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: QBR prep meeting for NEPTUNE on 2026-03-25T16:30:00Z.
